legend: Toni was walking through the wild CIn parking lot, dodging beasts and trying to find where he parked his car when he stumbled upon a formidable object: a stick of exact integer length n$$$n$$$.

Like any good problem-solver, Toni's mind immediately thought of a "gambiarra" (a makeshift solution). He needs to build a support base for his new hardware project. For the base to be stable, he needs to form a perfect triangle using pieces of this stick.
However, Toni is exhausted after a coding marathon. He decides to cut the stick at two distinct points, chosen completely at random. He only has energy for these two cuts.
Your mission is to calculate the chances of Toni's plan working, so he knows whether or not to give up and go grab a coffee.
Formally, we have a line segment of length n$$$n$$$. The set of possible cut points consists of the internal integer coordinates {1,2,…,n−1}$$$\{1, 2, \dots, n-1\}$$$.

Toni chooses two distinct cut points from this set, uniformly at random. This divides the original stick into three pieces with positive integer lengths a$$$a$$$, b$$$b$$$, and c$$$c$$$ (such that a+b+c=n$$$a+b+c = n$$$).
What is the probability that these three resulting pieces (a,b,c$$$a, b, c$$$) can form a non-degenerate triangle (i.e., a triangle with an area greater than zero)?

Since the answer can be an irreducible fraction pq$$$\frac{p}{q}$$$, you must print the value of p⋅q−1(mod109+7)$$$p \cdot q^{-1} \pmod{10^9 + 7}$$$, where q−1$$$q^{-1}$$$ is the modular inverse of q$$$q$$$ modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤105$$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. Each of the following t$$$t$$$ lines contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (3≤n≤109$$$3 \le n \le 10^9$$$), representing the length of the stick Toni found in that specific scenario.
output: For each test case, print a single integer on a new line: the probability of the makeshift solution working, modulo 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$.

legend.ai: Toni 正穿过荒野般的 CIn 停车场，一边躲避野兽，一边寻找自己停车的位置，途中偶然发现了一件了不起的东西：一根长度恰好为 n$$$n$$$ 的木棍。
像任何优秀的问题解决者一样，Toni 立刻想到了一个“gambiarra”（权宜之计）。他需要为自己的新硬件项目搭建一个支撑底座。为了让底座稳固，他需要用这根木棍的几段拼成一个完美的三角形。
然而，Toni 在经历了一场编程马拉松后已经筋疲力尽。他决定在两个不同的位置切断木棍，这两个位置完全随机选取。他只剩下力气切这两次。
你的任务是计算 Toni 的计划成功的概率，这样他就能知道自己是否该放弃，然后去喝杯咖啡。
严格地说，我们有一条长度为 n$$$n$$$ 的线段。可能的切点集合由内部整数坐标 {1,2,…,n−1}$$$\{1, 2, \dots, n-1\}$$$ 构成。
Toni 从该集合中等概率随机选择两个不同的切点。这会将原木棒分成三段，长度分别为正整数 a$$$a$$$、b$$$b$$$ 和 c$$$c$$$(满足 a+b+c=n$$$a+b+c = n$$$)。
这三段最终得到的木棒(a、b、c$$$a, b, c$$$)能够组成非退化三角形(即面积大于零的三角形)的概率是多少？
由于答案可以表示为最简分数 pq$$$\frac{p}{q}$$$，你需要输出 p⋅q−1(mod109+7)$$$p \cdot q^{-1} \pmod{10^9 + 7}$$$ 的值，其中 q−1$$$q^{-1}$$$ 是 q$$$q$$$ 在模 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$ 意义下的模逆元。

input.ai: 输入第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤105$$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$)——测试用例的数量。接下来的 t$$$t$$$ 行中，每行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(3≤n≤109$$$3 \le n \le 10^9$$$)，表示 Toni 在该场景中找到的木棒长度。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，在新的一行输出一个整数：临时方案成功的概率对 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$ 取模后的结果。
